result:
`final.py` scores **65.1** on the search split, against about 1.0 for the baseline. I used **2 of the 24** scorer calls, and both runs were valid.

| Version | Search score | CPU time (reference 1.32 s) |
|---|---|---|
| First version | 61.8 | 0.0214 s |
| Final (`final.py`) | 65.1 | 0.0203 s |

The baseline compared every pair of records. The new version uses prefix filtering, which only compares pairs that could possibly reach 80 % similarity:
- It ranks every word by how often it appears in the catalogue, rarest first, and processes records from fewest words to most.
- For each record it looks up only its first few rarest words in an index of the records already processed. That number is the word count minus `ceil(0.8 × word count)`, plus 1. Any pair that is at least 80 % alike must share at least one of those words.
- It skips candidates with too few words to reach 80 %. It then checks each remaining pair with the reference's exact integer test, `5·|A∩B| ≥ 4·|A∪B|`, so it reports exactly the same pairs.

Before scoring, I checked it against the reference on 300 random small inputs with edge cases (empty records, repeated words, very few distinct words) and on one larger input of about 2,300 records. Every result matched exactly.

I stopped after two scorer calls because the gain from the second version was small (61.8 to 65.1). At about 20 ms, much of the remaining time is probably fixed overhead, so I don't expect much more from further tuning.
